study.title: Acupuncture Modulation of Chronic Neuropathic Pain and Its Association With Brain Functional Properties
study.article_type: randomized controlled trial with neuroimaging substudy
study.study_design: exploratory study; randomized controlled trial with two parallel arms (acupuncture group and sham acupuncture group); multicenter
study.randomization: randomization sequence generated using software SAS 9.3 with a block of 6 by an independent researcher; random number communicated to acupuncturist via mobile phone message
study.blinding: patients blinded to group assignments; acupuncturists not blinded; other researchers blinded to treatment allocation
study.population: chronic sciatica patients aged 18-75 years, right-handed, with unilateral radiating leg pain below the knee for more than 3 months
study.inclusion_criteria: 1) age between 18 and 75 years; 2) having unilateral radiating leg pain below the knee for more than 3 months (not including patients exhibiting symptoms in both legs), accompanied by positive straight-leg raise test or corresponding neurological deficit (paresthesia, muscle weakness, or reflex abnormalities) with MRI or computed tomography-confirmed disk herniation; 3) leg pain intensity over 40 mm on a 0 to 100 mm visual analog scale (VAS); and 4) right-handed, in order to rule out the influence of handedness on the neuroimaging results
study.exclusion_criteria: 1) sciatica induced by other diseases than lumbar disk herniation; 2) having a severe spinal disease or severe progressive neurological symptoms; 3) having cardiovascular, liver, kidney, hematopoietic system diseases, mental health disorders, or other severe coexisting diseases; 4) pregnant or lactating women or those planning to conceive during the trial; 5) taking drugs that have a therapeutic effect on sciatica; 6) having had lumbar disk surgery within the past 1 year; 7) planning to receive surgery or interventional treatment during the treatment period; 8) having received acupuncture for sciatica within the past 1 year; and 9) had contraindications to MRI scan
study.source_location: pages 1-3, Abstract, Methods: Study Design, Participants

arms.dropouts: 5 discontinued: 3 unwillingness due to the epidemic, 2 had no time to receive treatment
5 discontinued: 2 dissatisfied with treatment effect, 2 unwillingness due to the epidemic, 1 had no time to receive treatment

extraction_notes.note: Supplementary Table 1 (adjunct acupoints for AG) and Supplementary Table 2 (non-acupoints for SG with full anatomical details) are referenced but not included in the provided PDF. Exact locations and coordinates of all 7 non-acupoints and all adjunct acupoints cannot be fully verified from the main text alone.

Deqi was described as intended in the AG but no formal quantitative measurement of deqi sensations (e.g., MASS or NRS subscales) was reported. The paper does not state that deqi was formally assessed.

The paper does not report expectancy ratings. Blinding was assessed via the James blinding index and participant guessing, but no formal expectancy or credibility instrument (e.g., Credibility/Expectancy Questionnaire) was used.
extraction_notes.source_location: page 4, Clinical Outcomes; page 5, Clinical Outcomes

extraction_notes.note: Table 1 reports VAS for back pain for AG as median (IQR) = 52.00 (44.50, 65.00) and for SG as mean (SD) = 53.84 (16.13), suggesting different distributional properties between groups for this variable. The statistical test footnote indicates nonparametric Mann-Whitney U was used (p = .580), consistent with non-normal distribution in at least one group.

Age for the AG is reported as mean (SD) = 42.88 (16.84) and for SG as median [IQR] = 28.00 (22.50, 56.50) in Table 1, with a footnote indicating nonparametric Mann-Whitney U test (p = .409). This suggests the distributions differ between groups, with the SG having a considerably different central tendency.

The paper states that 30 patients from a previously published multicenter RCT (ChiCTR2100044585) contributed data, and an additional 30 were recruited specifically for this neuroimaging study. The exact breakdown of how many of the 50 analyzed patients came from each source is not provided in the main text.

VAS for leg pain prediction model was not successfully established. The paper states only that the fALFF value of the SPL at baseline was found to be weakly correlated with 4-week VAS for leg pain in Spearman analysis, and no baseline clinical measure was significantly associated with VAS for leg pain at week 4. No quantitative r or p values for this weak Spearman correlation are given in the text.
extraction_notes.source_location: page 6, Primary Outcome Prediction Results; Figure 5A

extraction_notes.note: Figure 5A shows a Pearson correlation r matrix and Spearman correlation rho matrix. Some individual r and rho values are partially readable from the figure description but cannot be precisely extracted due to figure resolution limitations. The values are referenced as color-coded matrices and may not be fully reproducible from the text alone.

The paper mentions within-group changes (pre vs post) are depicted in Figure 3 box plots for VAS for leg pain (P<0.001 for both AG and SG pre-post), ODI (P<0.001 for AG, P=0.246 for SG), VAS for back pain (P<0.001 for AG, P=0.019 for SG), SFBI for bothersomeness (P<0.001 for AG, P=0.231 for SG), and SFBI for frequency (P<0.001 for AG, P=0.059 for SG). These within-group p-values are from the figure caption and boxes in Figure 3 and are not separately tabulated.

The coordinate space is stated as MNI (Montreal Neurological Institute) in the fALFF Analysis methods section. Peak MNI coordinates are reported in Table 3. This is consistent and treated as reported, not inferred.

The paper uses the term 'mixed-effects analysis' for between-group neuroimaging comparisons but does not specify the exact statistical model (e.g., repeated measures ANOVA, LME). The group-by-time interaction structure is implied but not fully detailed.

The paper does not report fALFF values at baseline or post-treatment as absolute numeric group means in a table. Figure 4B and 4D show box plots of right SPL and right PoCG fALFF values pre/post in AG and SG, but numeric values from these box plots are not extractable from the text.
The recruitment period (March 2021 to September 2022) spanned the COVID-19 pandemic, which caused some dropouts. This may limit generalizability and was noted as a limitation in the paper.
